subtopic: Cohort Retention Analysis and Survival Curves
question_text: [Data Storytelling & Business Metrics - Q25] In non-parametric survival analysis, how does the Kaplan-Meier estimator handle right-censored observation subjects?

options.text: It treats censored subjects as having experienced the event at the end of the study
It discards all censored subjects from the study cohort
It keeps subjects in the risk set up to their censoring timestamp, recalculating conditional survival probability only at known event times
It assumes event times follow an exponential hazard function

answer_explanation: Kaplan-Meier estimates S(t) = Prod (1 - d_i / n_i). Censored subjects remain in the denominator risk set n_i until their censoring point, avoiding biased attrition estimates.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: C. Rationale: Kaplan-Meier estimates S(t) = Prod (1 - d_i / n_i). Censored subjects remain in the denominator risk set n_i until their censoring point, avoiding biased attrition estimates.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
